newsitem.title: ITALY: Merrill says made no investment in Italian club.
newsitem.headline: Merrill says made no investment in Italian club.

text.p: U.S. bank Merrill Lynch said on Thursday that it had not made any investment on its own account in Italian Serie B soccer club Torino Calcio but was acting as a trustee on behalf of unnamed investors.

Richard Silverman, a spokesman for Merrill Lynch in London, said: "We have no investment in Torino football club and no management involvement. An undetermined number of private investors have decided to invest in the club through a Merrill Lynch trust account.
"We are acting as a trustee and a facilitator. We are not an investor," he added.

A company called Bullfin issued a statement in Turin on Wednesday saying that Merrill Lynch and Bankers Trust each had acquired a one-third stake in Bullfin, which had been created as a vehicle to take control of Torino.

The statement said that Bullfin, in which an Italian company called HSL had taken a 34 percent stake, had bought 88.39 percent of the soccer club for slightly more than 20 billion lire ($11.8 million) from its current chairman Gian Marco Calleri.

Two Italian businessmen linked to HSL -- Massimo Vidulich and Davide Palazzetti -- would take over the management of Torino, Vidulich as chairman and Palazzetti as Managing Director, the statement added.
A spokeswoman for Bankers Trust in London said on Thursday that an affiliate based in Jersey, BT Trustees Jersey Ltd, had bought 33 percent of Bullfin and would be managing the stake.
Asked whether the stake was being held in trust on behalf of other investors, the spokeswoman declined to comment.
